issues.description: Method signature mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(): The problem statement and UML specify a parameterless method SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() with signature +checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implementation declares public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This changes the public API: students following the specification will implement a parameterless method, while the solution (and its internal callers) use a boolean parameter. This inconsistency can confuse students, break direct comparisons with the reference solution, and lead to failing automated checks that expect the parameterless signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by exposing a parameterless public method. Option A (recommended): change the public API to public void checkOrderReady() and, if debug control is needed, implement a private helper private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) that the public method delegates to (e.g., checkOrderReady(false)). Update all internal calls (e.g., orderMeal) to call the parameterless checkOrderReady(). Option B: if keeping a boolean parameter is required, update the problem statement and UML to declare checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and explain the parameter's purpose. Prefer Option A to preserve the original exercise API while keeping internal debugging capability.
